title: AMD’s stock is getting hurt by this ‘unpalatable’ reality
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) shares are underperforming compared to other AI stocks in 2024, despite boosting its full-year AI revenue forecast. The reason for the muted performance is AMD's overall revenue outlook for the fourth quarter, which fell short of analyst expectations. This "unpalatable" reality contrasts with the strong growth seen in other AI-focused companies, according to one analyst.

title: Opinion: AMD’s AI event lacked a wow factor, but here’s one reason investors should be excited
summary: AMD's recent AI event, while lacking new customer announcements, gave investors a key reason for optimism: CEO Lisa Su's updated forecast for the AI accelerator chip market. Su now projects the market to reach over $500 billion by 2028, a significant increase from her previous forecast and representing an approximately 60% compounded annual growth rate from last year's $45 billion market. This revised outlook indicates strong anticipated growth in the AI sector.

title: AMD’s stock has a big catalyst on the horizon. Can it live up to the hype?
summary: AMD's stock is poised for a potential rally following its upcoming Advancing AI event, where new product announcements, including the MI325X artificial-intelligence accelerator, are expected. While AMD's stock has underperformed the broader chip sector this year, investors are looking to CEO Lisa Su and her team to provide a significant catalyst similar to last year's event. The event is anticipated to cover news on AMD's CPUs, GPUs, and its broader software ecosystem.

title: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) rose by 2.65% to $119.88 on Tuesday, outperforming the broader market. This positive performance occurred on a strong trading day where the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also saw significant gains. The stock closed below its 52-week high of $132.83, which was achieved on June 13th.

title: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) shares fell by 5.52% on Wednesday to $96.06, underperforming the broader stock market, which also experienced a rough trading session. The S&P 500 Index dropped 1.43%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.32%. AMD's closing price was $36.78 below its 52-week high of $132.83, achieved in June.

title: AMD, Broadcom stocks both drop for seventh straight session
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) and Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) experienced their seventh consecutive day of stock losses on Monday, marking their worst losing streaks since 2022. AMD shares fell 2.3% to close at $107.51, which is 33.6% below their record high from November 2021.

title: Opinion: AMD stock is sliding after earnings, and these numbers show why
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock slid significantly after the company reported a first-quarter net loss of $139 million and a revenue decline to $5.3 billion. This downturn was largely attributed to substantial drops in PC sales and gaming, exacerbated by a big decline in profit for its key data-center group and an unoptimistic forecast. The chip maker's overall margin was severely impacted, leading to a nearly 7% drop in its shares in after-hours trading.

title: AMD wins nearly a third of processor market, Arm's climb slows: analyst report
summary: AMD has significantly increased its market share in central processor units, capturing nearly a third of the x86 processor market from Intel, according to a recent analyst report from Mercury Research. This growth occurred during the worst PC chip market downturn since the 1980s. Meanwhile, Arm's rise in the PC market, primarily driven by Apple's Mac computers, slowed in the fourth quarter of 2022.

title: Why AMD is faring much better than Intel in the same tough economy
summary: AMD is showing a much brighter short-term outlook compared to Intel, despite both operating in a difficult chip market. While Intel faces widespread declines, AMD's data center business is experiencing growth, aided by new chip introductions and its acquisition of Xilinx. Both companies are affected by a slumping PC market, but AMD expects to gain market share in that segment and grow its data center revenue at Intel's expense this year.

title: AMD earnings face even more scrutiny after ‘astonishingly bad’ Intel outlook
summary: AMD's upcoming earnings report is under increased scrutiny following Intel's "astonishingly bad" outlook, particularly regarding inventory and data-center issues. CEO Lisa Su had previously expressed confidence that AMD would end 2022 in a stronger position, and the market will now evaluate that claim in light of rival Intel's struggles. AMD is scheduled to report its results after market close on Tuesday.

title: AMD can keep eating Intel’s lunch, Barclays says as stock surges
summary: Barclays upgraded AMD's stock to overweight from equal weight, leading to a more than 6% surge in AMD shares. Analyst Blayne Curtis believes AMD's Genoa and Bergamo platforms will enable further market-share gains against Intel. The upgrade also suggests AMD could benefit from Meta reaccelerating its spending.

title: AMD poaches Marvell’s Jean Hu for CFO slot as Devinder Kumar retires
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. announced that its financial chief Devinder Kumar is retiring, and Jean Hu from Marvell Technology Inc. will take his place as CFO. Marvell confirmed Hu's departure effective January 20, while AMD expects Hu to start on January 23. This change marks a significant leadership transition for AMD's financial department.

title: AMD launches data center CPU 'Genoa', taps Google, Microsoft as customers (Nov. 10)
summary: AMD has launched its fourth-generation EPYC processor, codenamed "Genoa," for data centers, securing major customers like Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle. This new chip offers significant performance and energy efficiency improvements over its predecessor, translating into lower operational costs for enterprises and cloud data centers. The launch comes as rival Intel faces delays with its own data center chip, and AMD continues to gain market share, boosting its stock by about 14%.

title: AMD amends GlobalFoundries deal, will buy $2.1 bln worth of wafers
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) has amended its agreement with GlobalFoundries, committing to purchase approximately $2.1 billion worth of silicon wafers between 2022 and 2025. This updated deal expands upon a previous agreement to buy $1.6 billion worth of chips from 2022 to 2024. Although AMD relies on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co for its most critical "chiplets," GlobalFoundries, a former AMD spin-off, continues to supply components to tie their chips together.

title: AMD sales rise 54% on strong demand for chips for servers and game consoles
summary: AMD reported strong third-quarter earnings, beating analyst expectations for both revenue and EPS, driven by high demand for its chips in PCs, servers, and game consoles. The company also issued a robust forecast for the fourth quarter, expecting continued growth in server and semi-custom segments amidst ongoing chip shortages. AMD's strategic acquisition of Xilinx is proceeding, aiming to strengthen its position in the data center market.

title: Hey Intel, AMD’s CEO is also ready to ‘fight for every socket,’ while producing strong growth
summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su responded to Intel's promise to "fight for every socket" by stating AMD is also ready for the competition. This comes as AMD demonstrates strong growth, particularly with data-center sales exceeding 20% of its revenue, leading to an increase in its annual guidance. Su's comments highlight the escalating rivalry in the chip market, particularly in the crucial data-center segment.

title: Intel in talks to buy GlobalFoundries for about $30 billion - WSJ
summary: Intel Corp is reportedly in talks to acquire semiconductor manufacturer GlobalFoundries Inc for approximately $30 billion, according to the Wall Street Journal. This potential deal comes amid a global semiconductor shortage and could help Intel significantly ramp up chip production, although GlobalFoundries has denied direct discussions with Intel. The acquisition could also raise antitrust questions given GlobalFoundries' history with AMD.

title: Intel vs. AMD — should you buy either stock now?
summary: This article contrasts Intel and AMD, two dominant players in the processor market, from an investment perspective. While AMD has shown significant outperformance under CEO Lisa Su, Intel remains the largest provider of core processors for PCs and servers, boasting a substantial R&D budget and strong cash flow. The piece questions which stock is a better buy for investors, acknowledging Intel's new CEO Pat Gelsinger's efforts to diversify and fend off AMD's market share gains.

title: Intel to spend $20 billion on U.S. chip plants as CEO challenges Asia dominance
summary: Intel announced plans to invest $20 billion in two new chip manufacturing plants in Arizona, aiming to expand its advanced chip production and open its factories to outside customers. This move by CEO Pat Gelsinger directly challenges the dominance of TSMC and Samsung in the advanced chip market and seeks to shift the technological balance of power back to the U.S. and Europe. The company expects $72 billion in revenue and adjusted earnings per share of $4.55 for 2021, and the new strategy is intended to restore Intel's reputation and create 3,000 permanent jobs.

title: Intel shares rise after Third Point urges chipmaker to explore strategic alternatives as market share deteriorates
summary: Hedge fund Third Point, which recently acquired a significant stake in Intel, is urging the chipmaker's board to explore strategic alternatives due to deteriorating market share against rivals like TSMC, Samsung, and AMD. Third Point highlighted concerns about Intel's loss of manufacturing leadership and its impact on U.S. national security. Intel has stated it welcomes input from investors to enhance shareholder value.

title: AMD Agrees to Buy Rival Chip Maker Xilinx for $35 Billion - WSJ
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) plans to acquire Xilinx Inc. for $35 billion in an all-stock deal, intensifying consolidation in the semiconductor industry. This acquisition is expected to significantly broaden AMD's product offerings and market reach, providing an immediate financial boost upon closure. The Wall Street Journal had previously reported on the impending agreement between the two rival chip makers.

title: Opinion: How did Intel lose its Silicon Valley crown?
summary: This article discusses Intel's decline as the leading chip manufacturer in Silicon Valley, examining whether the challenges stem from technological limits or leadership decisions. The chip giant announced a delay in its 7-nanometer manufacturing process and considered outsourcing some production for a key next-generation chip, shocking investors and analysts. This move is seen as a significant setback for the company once considered the standard-bearer of Moore's Law.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | AMD Is in Advanced Talks to Buy Xilinx
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire rival chip maker Xilinx Inc. The potential deal could be valued at over $30 billion, marking a significant consolidation in the semiconductor industry. This acquisition would enhance AMD's competitive position against Intel and expand its presence in telecommunications and defense markets.

title: AMD closes just shy of $100-billion market cap, as more analysts see it taking market share from Intel
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc.'s stock reached fresh records on Tuesday, closing with a market cap of $99.84 billion, just shy of $100 billion. This surge followed an analyst's price target hike and strong earnings reports, indicating an accelerating market share gain from Intel Corp. The company briefly surpassed a $100 billion market cap intraday.

title: Here are 2019’s biggest stock market winners and losers in the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq
summary: This article reviews the biggest stock market winners and losers across the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq for 2019 up to August 29th. It highlights top performers like Chipotle, AMD, Apple, and Visa, and notes disappointing results for Macy’s and Kraft Heinz. Despite ongoing media narratives, the U.S. stock market has shown strong returns year-to-date, with the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite Index all posting significant gains.

title: AMD stock rebounds from earnings disappointment with new server chip
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) shares are rising following optimism over its new second-generation Epyc 2 server chip, codenamed Rome. AMD announced that Rome offers nearly double the performance of Intel Corp.'s Xeon processor at approximately half the cost. This news comes after the company's recent earnings disappointment and could potentially impact Intel's stock.

title: AMD stock jumps 10% after detailing new PC push at trade show
summary: AMD's stock surged nearly 10% after the chip maker detailed new product launches at a trade show in Taiwan. An analyst noted that AMD's new CPU represents the first time the company has taken the process-technology and performance lead from Intel in desktop CPUs. This strong performance comes as AMD begins to deliver on its promise of new products in the second half of the year.

title: Opinion: AMD and Cray seek to develop fastest supercomputer in the world
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Cray Inc. have secured a $600 million contract from the U.S. Department of Energy to develop Frontier, which is expected to be the world's fastest supercomputer. This deal marks an ambitious revival of their partnership, potentially boosting AMD's influence in high-performance computing and data-center chips. Cray previously used AMD CPUs but switched to Intel, only to renew ties after AMD's Epyc data-center processors launched last year.

title: Intel CEO Bob Swan on the company's disappointing Q1 earnings
summary: Intel CEO Bob Swan discussed the company's disappointing Q1 earnings and a projected drop in revenue during an appearance on "Squawk on the Street." He also addressed pressure from China affecting the company's performance. The discussion provides insight into the challenges Intel was facing at the time.

title: Why Apple was so upset with Qualcomm — and why it finally had to give in
summary: Apple and Qualcomm settled a bitter legal battle over royalties and licensing fees, leading Apple to once again buy Qualcomm chips. The dispute centered on Qualcomm's patent licensing model, which Apple viewed as abusive due to its "no license, no chips" policy and pricing based on the total device cost. Despite Apple's strong objections and Qualcomm's history of antitrust issues, Apple ultimately settled because Qualcomm remains the leader in wireless technology, especially with the rollout of 5G networks, leaving Apple with few alternatives after Intel's exit from the 5G chip market.

title: Intel beats on revenue, slashes foundry investments as CEO says 'no more blank checks'
summary: Intel reported Q2 2025 earnings that beat Wall Street revenue expectations but announced significant cuts in chip factory construction and investments. CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated there would be "no more blank checks," emphasizing that every investment must make economic sense, particularly after the company invested too much in its foundry division without adequate demand. Intel's shares are up 13% year-to-date after a 60% plummet in 2024, and the company completed planned layoffs, reducing its workforce by 15%.

title: Intel’s stock-market run is unlike anything it’s seen in more than two decades
summary: Intel's stock has experienced its most significant three-day percentage gain since April 2001, rising 17.7% in three days, including a 7.2% jump on Wednesday. This rally is attributed to a favorable political environment and positive analyst commentary regarding its CPU business.

title: US plans to reduce Intel's $8.5 billion federal chips grant below $8 billion - New York Times
summary: The U.S. government plans to reduce Intel Corp's preliminary $8.5 billion federal chips grant to less than $8 billion, as reported by the New York Times. This adjustment factors in a $3 billion contract offered to Intel for manufacturing chips for the Pentagon. The initial grant was part of a larger government effort to boost domestic semiconductor production through the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act.

title: Cerence CEO Stefan Ortmanns to Depart; Ex-Intel Chief Krzanich Named as Replacement
summary: Cerence CEO Stefan Ortmanns is stepping down and will be replaced by Brian Krzanich, former chief of Intel and CDK Global. This change comes as the company undergoes a restructuring aimed at cost reduction. Ortmanns is recognized for his role in transitioning Cerence into a public company after its split from Nuance Communications in 2019.

title: Intel stock sinks more than 10% as early 2024 outlook comes up short
summary: Intel's stock dropped over 10% after the company issued a first-quarter 2024 outlook that fell short of analyst estimates, despite beating Wall Street expectations for the latest quarter. While CEO Pat Gelsinger stated the core PC and server chip businesses are healthy, overall sales are impacted by weakness in subsidiaries like Mobileye and its programmable chip unit. The company also broke a seven-quarter streak of declining revenue, with a 10% sales growth in Q4 2023.

title: Intel Corp. stock falls Friday, underperforms market
summary: Shares of Intel Corp. (INTC) fell 1.09% on Friday, closing at $47.12. This underperformed the broader market, which saw the S&P 500 Index rise slightly and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fall. The stock closed $4.16 below its 52-week high of $51.28 reached in late December.

title: Intel’s $25 billion investment in Israel ‘important and significant’ says country’s finance minister
summary: Intel Corp. is making a $25 billion investment in Israel, which the country's government has described as "important and significant." This investment follows Intel securing $3.2 billion in incentives from Israel. The funds will support a new chip manufacturing plant in Kiryat Gat, expected to begin operations by 2028 and create thousands of jobs.

title: Intel Corp. stock falls Monday, underperforms market
summary: Intel Corp. (INTC) shares fell 1.62% to $38.23 on Monday, underperforming a mixed market session where the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose and the S&P 500 Index declined slightly. The stock closed $1.84 below its 52-week high established in September.

title: China's Zeekr reveals wider loss in US IPO paperwork, Geely shares fall
summary: China's Zeekr Intelligent revealed wider losses for the first half of the year as it made its US IPO paperwork public, intending to use the funds to expand its product line. Shares in its parent company, Geely, fell on the news. Zeekr reported a net loss of 3.87 billion Chinese yuan ($531.34 million) for the six months ended June 30, though net revenue more than doubled.

title: Intel stock rallies after earnings show AI data-center beat, strong PC sales
summary: Intel's stock surged after reporting a surprise profit in its second-quarter earnings. While data-center sales exceeded expectations, the significant beat in PC product sales was the primary driver of improved gross margins. Shares rose by approximately 8% in extended trading following the announcement.

title: Intel Corp. stock rises Monday, outperforms market
summary: Intel Corp. (INTC) stock rose 3.68% on Monday, closing at $34.37. This performance outpaced the broader market, as the S&P 500 Index increased by 0.39% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.22%. The rise marked the end of a two-day losing streak for Intel.

title: Chipmaker Micron beats on demand from booming AI, easing glut
summary: Micron Technology exceeded third-quarter revenue estimates driven by high demand for its memory chips in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence sector and an easing supply glut in traditional markets. The company's shares rose over 2% after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings and anticipating improved pricing trends. Despite ongoing U.S.-China tech tensions impacting its presence in the Chinese market, Micron expressed confidence in the memory industry's recovery.

title: Applied Materials stock rises on new chip-making system that helps lower costs
summary: Applied Materials Inc. shares rose after the company unveiled a new chip-making system designed to lower manufacturing costs for semiconductors. The system, called Centura Sculpta, promises to save fabs like TSMC and Intel $50 per wafer. This innovation led to a notable outperformance of Applied Materials stock compared to its peers and the broader semiconductor market.

title: Intel cuts dividend to lowest since 2007 to save cash
summary: Intel Corp has cut its quarterly dividend payout by 66% to $0.125 per share, the lowest level since 2007, to conserve cash. This decision comes as the company faces slowing demand for its chips amid a deteriorating macro-economic environment and aims to scale back major investments in manufacturing equipment. CEO Pat Gelsinger indicated the move was necessary to prioritize capital for its foundry business and achieve significant cost reductions by 2025.

title: Exclusive: Intel weighs boost to investment in Vietnam chip packaging plant
summary: Intel Corp is reportedly considering a significant increase, possibly around $1 billion, to its existing $1.5-billion investment in Vietnam to expand its chip testing and packaging plant. This potential move highlights Vietnam's growing importance in the global semiconductor supply chain, as companies seek to diversify away from China and Taiwan due to geopolitical risks. While other locations like Singapore and Malaysia are also being considered, an expansion in Vietnam would help Intel manage supply disruptions and align with Vietnam's aggressive push to grow its chipmaking industry.

AMD is scheduled to report its results after market close on Tuesday.

title: Opinion: Intel just had its worst year since the dot-com bust, and it won’t get better anytime soon
summary: Intel faced its worst financial year since 2001, with annual earnings declining over 60% and revenue dropping more than 20% in 2022. This downturn is attributed to a slump in both PC sales and data centers, with executives forecasting further declines. The company is also losing market share to AMD, indicating a challenging period ahead.

title: Intel Chairman Omar Ishrak steps down
summary: Intel announced that Chairman Omar Ishrak has stepped down and Frank Yeary has been appointed as his replacement. Ishrak, who became chairman in 2020 and was instrumental in bringing CEO Pat Gelsinger back to the company, will continue to serve as an independent director on Intel's board. Yeary, a long-time Intel director, also serves on the boards of PayPal Holdings and Intel's Mobileye.

title: Apple to start using in-house screens from 2024 - Bloomberg News
summary: Apple plans to begin using its own custom displays in mobile devices starting in 2024, aiming to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Samsung and LG. The transition will start with high-end Apple Watches, followed by other devices including the iPhone, and will involve upgrading to microLED technology. This move is part of a broader strategy by Apple to bring more component production in-house, following similar shifts with chips from Broadcom and Intel.

title: Intel's Mobileye sees $17 bln in assisted-driving product revenues by 2030
summary: Intel Corp's self-driving tech unit, Mobileye Global Inc., projects over $17 billion in revenues from its advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) products by 2030. The company, a leading player in the ADAS market, also anticipates an additional $3.5 billion in revenues through 2028 from its autonomous mobility-as-a-service products. Mobileye expects the volume of its SuperVision product-based vehicles to reach 1.2 million units by 2026, driven by strong demand in China.

title: Intel delaying German factory start, wants more subsidies, Volksstimme reports
summary: Intel Corp has reportedly delayed the start of its chip factory in Magdeburg, Germany, seeking more public subsidies due to rising energy and raw materials costs. The original budget of 17 billion euros has increased to nearly 20 billion euros, and Intel cited geopolitical challenges and decreased semiconductor demand. The company is currently in discussions with the German government to bridge the funding gap.

title: AMD launches data center CPU 'Genoa', taps Google, Microsoft as customers (Nov. 10)
summary: AMD has launched its fourth-generation EPYC processor, codenamed "Genoa," for data centers, securing major customers like Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle. This new chip offers significant performance and energy efficiency improvements over its predecessor, translating into lower operational costs for enterprises and cloud data centers. The launch comes as rival Intel faces delays with its own data center chip, and AMD continues to gain market share, boosting its stock by about 14%.

title: Mobileye pops more than 37% in market debut after spinning out of Intel
summary: Mobileye, Intel's self-driving car technology company, saw its shares surge over 37% in its stock market debut after spinning out of Intel. The IPO, which valued Mobileye at around $17 billion, raised $861 million, with Intel planning to use some proceeds to build chip factories. This market debut provides a notable tech IPO in a slow year, despite Mobileye's valuation being below Intel's initial expectations.

title: Mobileye IPO: 5 things to know about the Intel autonomous-driving spinoff
summary: Intel's autonomous-driving spinoff Mobileye Global Inc. has returned to the public markets through an IPO, pricing shares at $21, above the targeted range. While Intel initially hoped for a valuation as high as $50 billion, Mobileye's market capitalization is now close to its original acquisition price of $15.3 billion at roughly $16.7 billion due to a struggling IPO market. Mobileye, a pioneer in automated-driving technology, is focusing on a larger market while facing increasing competition.

title: Intel CEO Pushes to Further Separate Chip-Design, Production Arms
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger is planning to further separate the company's chip-design and chip-making factory operations. This new structure is intended to allow Intel's factories to function as contract chip-making operations, serving both Intel engineers and external chip companies equally, as part of a broader effort to revamp the company and increase returns.

title: Intel Files IPO Plans for Its Mobileye Autonomous Driving Unit
summary: Intel has filed paperwork with the SEC for an initial public offering (IPO) of its Mobileye Global unit. Mobileye specializes in developing chips and software for autonomous driving systems. This move indicates Intel's strategy to spin off and potentially raise capital for its autonomous driving business.

title: Intel Gave CEO Pay Package Worth Nearly $180 Million Amid Turnaround Effort
summary: Intel's CEO, Pat Gelsinger, received a compensation package worth nearly $180 million for 2021, much of which is tied to the company's stock performance. This substantial pay aims to incentivize a significant turnaround at the chip giant. The package placed him as the second-highest-paid CEO among S&P 500 companies for the year.

title: Intel commits $36 billion to making chips in Europe
summary: Intel announced plans to invest over 33 billion euros ($36 billion) to boost chipmaking in the European Union, aiming to reduce the bloc's reliance on external semiconductor sources. This includes building two new factories in Magdeburg, Germany, creating an R&D and design hub in France, and investing in other European countries like Ireland, Italy, Poland, and Spain. The investment is part of Intel's broader commitment to spend up to 80 billion euros in Europe over the next decade, aligning with the EU's new European Chips Act to strengthen its semiconductor sector.

title: Intel delays 2023 server chip, says it needs to boost spending to catch competitors
summary: Intel announced it would need to significantly increase spending over the next two years to fund its turnaround and transformation into a semiconductor manufacturer. The company also confirmed that the release of its forthcoming server chip, codenamed Granite Rapids, has been pushed from 2023 to 2024. This delay and investment strategy led to a drop in Intel's stock as investors questioned the impact on profit margins and the capital-intensive nature of its new foundry business.

title: Virgin Galactic, Tower Semiconductor, CrowdStrike, Bitcoin: What to Watch in the Stock Market Today
summary: This article highlights key market movers, including Intel's acquisition of Tower Semiconductor, Arista Networks exceeding earnings expectations, and the gains in cybersecurity stocks due to potential cyberattack concerns. It also notes Bitcoin's rise and Virgin Galactic's upcoming public ticket sales, alongside mixed results for other major tech and hospitality companies.

title: Chip giants are ramping up spending by the billions as semiconductor demand booms
summary: Major semiconductor companies like TSMC and Intel are investing billions into new fabrication plants and research to meet the booming global demand for chips, despite the ongoing chip shortage. TSMC plans to spend $100 billion over three years, while Intel announced a $20 billion investment in Arizona. Analysts expect a "choppy" recovery from the shortage in the short term, but demand is projected to continue increasing, benefiting suppliers like ASML and Applied Materials.

title: Intel stock hits lowest price in more than a year, and there is another shoe to drop
summary: Intel's stock dropped over 6% to its lowest point in more than a year after analysts warned of potential troubles beyond falling margins: an impending oversupply of PCs. This oversupply is expected to severely impact Intel's largest business segment. The stock's performance made it the worst performer on the Dow Jones Industrial Average Thursday.

title: Intel stock punished again as slimmer profit margins ding earnings forecast, but CEO sticks to his plan
summary: Intel's stock was punished again after the company's earnings forecast was dinged by slimmer profit margins, despite CEO Gelsinger sticking to his long-term plan for building out manufacturing capacity. The chip maker expects profit margins to remain under pressure for an extended period, leading to a disappointing earnings guidance that fell below Wall Street expectations. Intel forecast GAAP gross margins of 49% and non-GAAP margins of 52% for the first quarter, with expected GAAP earnings of 70 cents a share and non-GAAP earnings of 80 cents a share.

title: Intel to build $20B Ohio chip facility amid global shortage
summary: Intel announced its plan to invest $20 billion in building a new chip manufacturing facility in Ohio to help address the global chip shortage and boost domestic production. The project, involving two factories, is expected to create thousands of jobs and establish a new technology hub. This significant investment is also intended to support U.S. national security by increasing the domestic supply of crucial microprocessors.

title: Al Gore’s Firm Bought Intel and Alibaba Stock. It Sold Texas Instruments.
summary: Al Gore's firm, Generation Investment Management, significantly adjusted its U.S.-traded investments in the third quarter. The firm doubled its stake in Intel and increased its holdings in Alibaba, while simultaneously reducing its position in Texas Instruments by half.

title: Investors are going wild over a Dutch chip firm. And you've probably never heard of it
summary: ASML, a Dutch chip firm, holds a critical monopoly in manufacturing the highly complex extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUV) machines essential for producing the most advanced chips. Despite its significant market value of $350 billion and being crucial to major chipmakers like TSMC, Samsung, and Intel, many investors may not be familiar with the company. Demand for ASML's machines is projected to lead to a significant sales boom over the next decade, with annual revenue expected to hit 24-30 billion euros by 2025.

title: How Intel plans to catch Samsung and TSMC and regain its dominance in the chip market
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has outlined an ambitious plan to regain dominance in the chip market by 2025, aiming to surpass competitors Samsung and TSMC. The strategy involves significant investment in new fabrication plants globally, totaling over $44 billion, and opening Intel's fabs to other companies through Intel Foundry Services. This move addresses past production missteps and aims to leverage government subsidies like the CHIPS Act to boost U.S. chip manufacturing.

title: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger hopes to win back Apple by outcompeting it
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger expressed his hope to regain Apple as a customer, acknowledging that Intel will need to outperform Apple to achieve this. Gelsinger stated that he doesn't blame Apple for choosing to produce its own chips over using Intel's. He emphasized the necessity of Intel's products being superior to Apple's.
